purpose: Teach: この世/イチゴ/味覚/いちご/訪ねる/アイロン/新生児/取り替え

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、この世、絶対、で、絶対、ばあさんが、絶対、お父さんの、絶対、宝物だったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, when you were young, you were truly Dad's greatest treasure — do you remember? I mean it.
lines.style: Soft opening. Voice full of reaching back. Warm but deliberate. Pauses slightly before 'do you remember' like testing whether to say it aloud. Ends with quiet certainty — not asking for reassurance, offering it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、イチゴ、絶対、お土産、絶対、よく、絶対、持ってきてくれたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes. When you were young, Grandpa would bring me strawberries as gifts all the time — you remember that, don't you, dear? I really do.
lines.style: Bright recognition at the start. Shifts to a gentle, almost sing-song warmth. Comfortable pause before 'all the time.' Ends with a small, contented sigh — not wistful, just satisfied that it happened.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、ばあさんの、絶対、お料理の、絶対、味覚、絶対、お父さん、絶対、大好きだったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, I really loved the taste of your cooking — do you remember? I mean it.
lines.style: Slower tempo than before. Eyes maybe looking away briefly. The affection carries weight now, almost vulnerable. Soft emphasis on 'the taste.' Trailing off slightly, like he's checking himself for being sentimental.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お庭の、絶対、いちご、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、収穫したわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, we would pick strawberries together from the garden, wouldn't we? Do you remember that, dear? I really do.
lines.style: Immediate warmth and lightness. Voice carries a small smile. Gentle rhythm like the action itself — steady, unhurried. 'Together' gets a soft emphasis. Ends with satisfied finality, not looking for agreement.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、ご親戚を、絶対、訪ねる、絶対、こと、絶対、お父さん、絶対、楽しみにしたぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, I looked forward to visiting relatives with such excitement — do you remember, Gran? I really mean that.
lines.style: Builds slightly toward 'excitement.' Voice opens up a little more than before. There's genuine warmth in the reaching back. The 'do you remember' is gentler, almost checking in. Ends with quiet conviction.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、ばあさん、絶対、お祖父ちゃんのシャツ、絶対、アイロン、絶対、毎日、絶対、かけたわよ、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, I would iron your shirts every single day — can you believe I did that, dear? I really did.
lines.style: Quick, warm laugh threaded through the opening. Slight self-aware humor about the care itself. Rhythm mimics the repetition of the action. Small lift on 'every single day.' Ends with tender amusement, not asking for sympathy.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お孫さんの、絶対、新生児、絶対、の、絶対、お顔、絶対、お父さん、絶対、見たぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, I saw our grandchild when they were just born — do you remember that, Gran? I really did.
lines.style: Sudden softness and slowness. Voice catches slightly on 'just born.' This is sacred ground. Pause before 'do you remember' — giving weight to the moment. Ends with quiet reverence, almost fragile.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、家具の、絶対、取り替え、絶対、お祖父ちゃんが、絶対、自分で、絶対、しましたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, you replaced all the furniture yourself with your own hands — don't you remember that, dear? You really did.
lines.style: Warm brightness with underlying pride. Slight emphasis on 'yourself.' Voice carries both affection and gentle teasing — recognizing his capability. Comfortable pace. Ends with a small satisfied finality.
